newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan electronics firms to boost mini-disc exports.
newsitem.headline: Japan electronics firms to boost mini-disc exports.

text.p: Sharp Corp, Hitachi Maxell Ltd and Sony Corp said on Thursday they will boost exports of mini-discs (MDs) to North America and Europe, where they see high growth potential.
MDs are audio discs that are smaller than compact discs (CD) and can be used for both recording and playing sound.
Sharp said it hopes to achieve a ten-fold increase in MD exports in the year ending in March 1998 to 500,000 units.
A Sharp spokesman said the firm expects its output of MDs to rise during 1997/98 to a monthly rate of 300,000 units from 200,000 units per month in 1996/97.
Sharp will also strengthen the marketing operations of its German and French units, he added.
Hitachi Maxell said it would invest 2.7 billion yen to construct a new MD production line in Japan, aiming to increase total output to 2.3 million units annually by March 1998.
The company expects to boost MD exports to 10 percent of total output in fiscal year 1997/98, compared with five percent in 1996/97.
Sony said it expects to export 750,000 MDs in 1997/98, compared with slightly fewer than 500,000 units a year earlier.
"Demand for MDs is expected to jump, especially in Europe, as there have been no new audio products since the introduction of CDs several years ago," a Sony spokesman said.
